newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt mkts close weaker, bulls seen in short end.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt mkts close weaker, bulls seen in short end.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.95 PCT (PREV 8.05) US 5-YR 6.14 (PREV 6.11)
* NZ yields end slightly higher as MPS still being felt
* Short end starts to shake blues, rally seen
* Bonds take lead from U.S., trade subdued as Xmas nears
New Zealand debt markets ended weaker on Wednesday but bank bills had started to shake the nervous sentiment provoked by a cautious Reserve Bank statement on Tuesday.
"It looked reasonably heavy this morning but it's come back pretty well bid," a dealer said of the short end.

At Tuesday's Monetary Policy Statement (MPS), Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash sanctioned the recent rally in the debt markets. But he also warned that the euphoric reaction to the formation of a centre-right coalition government last week was "somewhat excessive".
The New Zealand dollar spiked higher after the release of the MPS, peaking at US$0.7096 and 67.39 on its Trade-Weighted Index on Tuesday before easing back a touch.
Dealers said the strong currency was positive for the money market, and the 90-day bank bill yield was seen lower.
"As long as this Kiwi remains resonably strong, like it's looking to do at the moment, then I think at some stage we'll have a look at 7.75 (percent)," said one.
He said present conditions, with the Trade-Wieghted Index at around 67.40, were probably tighter than the Reserve Bank needed them to be.
On Tuesday Brash said the widening of the bank's target band for core inflation to 0-3 percent meant a mix of 90-day bills at 8.5 percent and the TWI at 66.5 was consistent with overall conditions.
But dealers noted Brash had also said the bank could accept conditions slightly looser or tighter than those levels.
Bond prices followed the U.S. market lower but dealers said trade had been quiet.
"I think most guys are happy to wind this week up and get into a bit of a festive mood," one dealer remarked.
